cards.prose: The man is in the synagogue on the day the commandment says to keep holy, and Yahusha (Jesus) does not put that commandment aside to help him. He puts the question to the room: *Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil?* (Mark 3:4). The day stands; what he refuses is the added rule that would have left the man as he was.
cards.member_sentence: The fourth commandment tells Yashar'el (Israel) to remember the sabbath day and keep it holy, the commandment Yahusha (Jesus) keeps while he heals.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) goes into the synagogue on the sabbath as a man keeping the day, and Moses gave that commandment a second time in Deuteronomy, *as Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath commanded thee*. The healing happens inside the keeping, in the assembly of the day, and not on his way out of it.
cards.member_sentence: Moses gives the sabbath commandment a second time in Deuteronomy, the day Yahusha (Jesus) keeps in the synagogue before he heals.

cards.prose: Here the Pharisees go out and plot with the Herodians to destroy the man who had just made a hand whole. John shows the same thing from the other end: after Lazarus is raised, the chief priests and Pharisees gather a council and ask *What do we?* because *this man doeth many miracles*. In both rooms the good that was done is the problem they meet to solve.
cards.member_sentence: After Lazarus is raised, the chief priests and Pharisees gather in council over the many miracles, as the Pharisees plotted over the withered hand.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) names twelve on the mountain, and twelve is the number of the tribes. Ezekiel is told to take two sticks, one for Yahudah (Judah) and one for the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the word is *join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand* (Ezekiel 37:17). Twelve men are sent out to a house that is to be made one again.
cards.member_sentence: This opens Ezekiel's word of the two sticks, Yahudah (Judah) and the house of Yashar'el (Israel), which Yahuah (the LORD) will join into one.

cards.prose: Revelation sets twelve gates in the wall of the holy city, and on them the names of *the twelve tribes*, and under the wall *twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb* (Revelation 21:14). The tribes are written on the gates and the men who were sent are written in the foundations, so the number Yahusha (Jesus) ordained on the mountain is the number the city is built on.
cards.member_phrase: twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon
cards.member_sentence: The city's wall has twelve gates with the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) written on them.

cards.prose: Here scribes from Jerusalem watch a man set free from unclean spirits and say his power is Beelzebub's. Yahusha (Jesus) says elsewhere what happens when a teaching puts its own handed-down tradition above the commandment: it makes the word of Elohim (God) of none effect. When the teaching of men matters more than the word, even a man made whole is read as a danger.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says the tradition of the elders makes the word of Elohim (God) of none effect, the habit on show when scribes call his work Beelzebub's.

cards.prose: Mark opens wide: every sin and every blasphemy shall be forgiven, and then he sets one thing outside that forgiveness. John draws a line of his own among sins. When a man sees his brother sin a sin not unto death, he asks and life is given, but there is *a sin unto death*, and John says he does not say to pray for it.
cards.member_phrase: There is a sin unto death: I do not say that he shall pray for it.
cards.member_sentence: John separates a sin unto death from the sins for which a brother may ask and be given life, and does not say to pray for that one.

cards.prose: Asked who his mother and brethren are, he looks round at those sitting with him and says that whoever does *the will of Elohim (God)* (Mark 3:35) is that family. Hosea gives the other side: those once told *Ye are not my people* are called *sons of the living Elohim (God)*, and the Father does the calling. The doing is how such sons are known when they stand before him; it is the Father who has named them.
cards.member_phrase: there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: Where the house of Yashar'el (Israel) was told it was not his people, it is told it is the sons of the living Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Mark's family is made of those who do *the will of Elohim (God)*, and Matthew has him say it in his own words at the end of the sermon: the door is for *he that doeth the will of my Father*. There the saying carries a warning against calling him Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord) without doing. The doing is what shows who belongs, whether he is naming his household or naming who enters.
cards.member_phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: Matthew has him say that not everyone who calls him Adonai (Lord) enters the kingdom, but the one who does the will of his Father.
